hypotheses.reasoning: session-cache node was replaced and restarted empty at 21:42:34 (#224) because no RDB snapshot was found. account-svc then saw miss ratios of 97-98% against a 4-5% baseline (#231, #235) and sent every lookup to accounts-db. The database saturated: connections reached 488-496/500 and CPU 94-97% (#232, #240). Simple primary-key lookups slowed to 3-8s (#243, #268), account-svc queries timed out at 5s (#254), and edge-proxy began returning 504s on /login from 21:44:45 (#241). Before the cache wipe, logins completed with 200 in about 100-170ms (#218-#230).
The same chain viewed as a cascade: losing the cache caused a thundering herd of reads on accounts-db, which made account-svc time out and edge-proxy return 504s.

There was one connection reset to the external identity provider at 21:31, 13 minutes before the 504s began, with nothing similar afterward. Likely a red herring. Other unrelated noise: audit_log seq scan (#201), audit-consumer GC pause (#205), edge-proxy disk warning (#57).

verdict.recommendedAction: Reduce load on accounts-db: rate-limit or queue cache refills in account-svc (single-flight/request coalescing) and pre-load hot session/account keys into session-cache. Temporarily shed /login load or raise the DB pool and add read capacity if possible. Afterwards, turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replication for session-cache so a node replacement doesn't start it empty, and add stampede protection.
